To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of GABA(A) receptor subunit m-RNAs in cultured neurons from chick embryo cerebral cortex changes in a developmentally-regulated fashion and in a GABA-agonist dependent manner.

(1) GABA(A) receptor mRNAs in cultured chick cortical neurons increase in abundance during maturation in vitro; (2) GABA(A)-receptor subunit mRNA levels are downregulated by GABA; and (3) the downregulation occurs with different time courses for the different subunit mRNAS.
1) GABA receptor subunit mRNAS are developmentally regulated and 2) GABA down-regulates the expression of these mRNAs in cultured neurons.
